ai.description: The Spinular Night Frog is 30–45 mm long with a brown, mottled dorsum. It is distinguished by prominent, spine-like tubercles covering the skin and a pointed snout. It is currently unassigned to a family.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus acanthodermis* is uniquely distinguished by the prominent, sharp, spine-like tubercles scattered across its dorsal skin, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Spinular Night Frog inhabits evergreen forests in the southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spinular Night Frog is primarily nocturnal and possesses unique, spine-like skin projections that may enhance camouflage or sensory perception in its habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus acanthodermis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), depositing small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in rock crevices or near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus acanthodermis* is endemic to the high-elevation evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Spinular Night Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "ticking" calls, typically heard emanating from rocky stream beds in its humid forest habitat.
